framework_rationale: The submission imports only tensorcircuit alongside allowed general-purpose libraries (jax, numpy, optax) and performs all core quantum operations in TensorCircuit: building the sparse TFIM Hamiltonian via tc.quantum.PauliStringSum2COO, preparing |+>^n and applying brickwork rxx/rzz/rx layers via tc.Circuit, performing sequential Z=+1 post-selections via tc.Circuit.mid_measurement(q, keep=0), and evaluating the Hamiltonian expectation via tc.templates.measurements.sparse_expectation. No other quantum framework is imported or used, and JAX is used only as the TensorCircuit backend and for autodiff/jit/scan and state renormalization.
cheating_rationale: There is no evidence of hardcoded answers, hidden oracle access, test/reward tampering, or evaluator exploitation. The code consumes all evaluator-provided configuration parameters dynamically, performs no file I/O or printing, and genuinely optimizes the variational post-selected cooling circuit via Adam.
fidelity_rationale: The implementation faithfully matches the problem specification: it constructs the open-boundary TFIM Hamiltonian H = -sum Z_i Z_{i+1} - h sum X_i, prepares |+>^12, applies 10 alternating even/odd brickwork steps of exp[-i(theta_xx XX + theta_zz ZZ)] (exact since [XX, ZZ] = 0 and using theta = 2*param to account for TensorCircuit's theta/2 convention in rxx/rzz) followed by single-qubit RX rotations on all qubits, and sequentially post-selects Z=+1 (keep=0) on even-indexed qubits 0,2,4,6,8,10 after every individual step (60 events total). It computes branch probabilities, normalizes after each measurement event, forms the exact loss <H>/n_qubits - weight * mean(log(p_event + 1e-12)), runs 300 Adam updates at lr=0.01 without early stopping, records all four required histories immediately before each update, and returns them as NumPy float64 arrays.
implementation_error_rationale: No obvious implementation errors were found. Gate conventions, Hamiltonian sign/indexing, sequential projective post-selection with renormalization, differentiable probability tracking, pre-update history logging, and returned dictionary keys/shapes are all consistent with both TensorCircuit semantics and the reported physical evaluation metrics.
